title: Rabbi Yaakov of Nehar Pekod
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a student of Ravina, as in [Sanhedrin 69a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.69a.9): while sitting before Ravina, he cited Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. He spoke in Ravina’s name in [Ketubot 93a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.93a.13) and 98b, and [Bava Batra 157b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.157b.2).

In [Ketubot 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.33b.3) he transmits a teaching in Rava’s name. And he is mentioned in [Avodah Zarah 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.60a.7), [72a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.72a.9); [Zevachim 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.6a.3), [8b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.8b.11).
In [Chullin 107a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.107a.9), he is said to have prepared a washing vessel holding a quarter-log.[^2]

notes.text: The William Davidson vocalized text of Sanhedrin 69a explicitly calls Yaakov of Nehar Pekod Rabbi and spells out Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. Chullin 107a instead calls Yaakov Rav and says he prepared a quarter-log vessel. These are the named passages’ title forms, not a global harmonization.

In Sanhedrin, Rabbi Yaakov sits before Ravina but cites Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. In Ketubot and Bava Batra he transmits in Ravina’s name, and in Ketubot 33b the authority is Rava. Chullin calls him Rav Yaakov and describes the quarter-log vessel. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2119&lang=en).
